1.1: These the names of Jacob's sons—the ones that moved to Egypt wit' him, each one bringing they whole fam.
1.5: Altogether, Jacob had seventy descendants in Egypt, including Joseph, who was already out there handling business.
1.6: Over time, Joseph and all his brothers passed away, ending that whole generation.
1.7: But their kids? Man, they multiplied like crazy, had a whole bunch of babies and grandbabies. The Israelites got so deep and strong they started filling up the whole land.
1.8: Then one day, a new Pharaoh came up in Egypt, and he ain't know nothing 'bout Joseph or what he did.
1.9: He told his people, 'Look, these Israelites? They outnumber us now and they stronger too.'
1.10: 'We gotta do something before they grow even bigger. If a war pop off, they gon' link up with our enemies, fight against us, and dip out this country.'
1.11: So the Egyptians made 'em slaves, put some ruthless bosses over them, tryna break their spirits with hard work. Made 'em build up the cities of Pithom and Rameses just to store Pharaoh's supplies.
1.12: But the crazier the Egyptians treated 'em, the more they kept growing and spreading. Egypt got real nervous.
1.13: So they worked the Israelites even harder, with no mercy at all.
1.14: Made life miserable for 'em—forced 'em to mix mortar, make bricks, work the fields, just straight-up ruthless with the demands.
1.15: Then Pharaoh, Egypt's king, called up two Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah.
1.16: He told 'em, 'When y'all help the Hebrew women give birth, watch close. If it's a boy, kill him. If it's a girl, let her live.'
1.17: But the midwives feared God, so they ain't listen to Pharaoh—they let the baby boys live too.
1.18: Pharaoh pulled them up and said, 'Why y'all let these boys live? What's up with that?'
1.19: They told him, 'The Hebrew women ain't like Egyptian women—they strong! They be popping them babies out fast, before we even get there.'
1.20: So God took care of the midwives, and the Israelites just kept multiplying, getting stronger and stronger.
1.21: Since the midwives feared God, He blessed them with families of their own.
1.22: Then Pharaoh took it to the next level—he told all his people, 'Every newborn Hebrew boy? Toss him in the Nile River. But y'all can let the girls live.'

2.1: Around this time, a man and woman from the tribe of Levi got married.
2.2: The woman got pregnant and had a son. When she saw how special he was, she hid him for three months.
2.3: But when she couldn't hide him no more, she got a basket made of papyrus reeds, sealed it up with tar and pitch, put the baby inside, and placed it in the reeds along the Nile River bank.
2.4: His sister stood at a distance, watching to see what would happen to him.
2.5: Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river to take a bath, while her attendants walked along the bank. She noticed the basket in the reeds and sent one of her maids to go get it.
2.6: She opened it up and saw the baby inside—he was crying, and she felt sorry for him. She said, 'This gotta be one of the Hebrew babies.'
2.7: Then the baby's sister stepped up and said, 'You want me to go find a Hebrew woman to nurse him for you?'
2.8: 'Yes, go!' the princess said. So the girl went and got the baby's mother.
2.9: Pharaoh's daughter told her, 'Take this baby and nurse him for me. I'll pay you for it.' So the woman took her son back home and nursed him.
2.10: When the boy got older, his mother brought him back to Pharaoh's daughter, who adopted him as her own. She named him Moses, saying, 'I lifted him out the water.'
2.11: Years later, when Moses was grown, he went out to see his people—the Hebrews—and saw how hard they was being worked. While he was out there, he saw an Egyptian beating one of his Hebrew brothers.
2.12: Moses looked around to make sure nobody was watching, then killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
2.13: The next day, Moses went back out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one in the wrong, 'Bruh, why you beating up your own brother?'
2.14: The man said, 'Who put you in charge? You our prince now? You gon' kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?'
2.15: Moses got scared, thinking, 'Dang, people know what I did.' Sure enough, Pharaoh heard about it and tried to kill Moses. But Moses ran away to Midian and stayed there.
2.16: When Moses got to Midian, he sat down next to a well. The priest of Midian had seven daughters who came to draw water for their father's flock, just like they always did.
2.17: But some other shepherds came through and tried to push them out the way. Moses wasn't having it—he jumped up, helped the girls, and made sure their flock got watered.
2.18: When the girls got back home to their father, Reuel, he said, 'Y'all back early today! What happened?'
2.19: They told him, 'An Egyptian helped us out! He ran off the shepherds and then watered our flock for us.'
2.20: 'Where he at then?' Reuel asked. 'Why'd y'all leave him out there? Go invite him to dinner!'
2.21: Moses accepted the invite and ended up staying with them. After a while, Reuel gave him his daughter Zipporah as his wife.
2.22: Later on, she had a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I been a foreigner in a land that ain't mine.'
2.23: Years went by, and the Pharaoh who wanted Moses dead finally died. But the Israelites was still suffering under slavery, crying out for help. Their cries went up to God.
2.24: God heard their pain and remembered His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
2.25: He looked down on Israel and knew—it was time to move.

3.1: One day, Moses was out tending the flock of his father-in-law, Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock deep into the wilderness and came up to Sinai, God's mountain.
3.2: Outta nowhere, an angel of the Lord showed up in a blazing fire right in the middle of a bush. Moses looked, and he was shook—'cause even though the bush was on fire, it wasn't burning up!
3.3: Moses was like, 'Man, this wild! Why this bush ain't burning up? I gotta go check this out.'
3.4: When the Lord saw Moses getting closer, He called out from the bush, 'Moses! Moses!'
3.6: God said, 'Don't come no closer. Take off your sandals, 'cause you standin' on holy ground.'
3.7: Then He said, 'I'm the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Soon as Moses heard that, he covered his face, 'cause he was scared to even look at God.
3.8: Then the Lord said, 'I seen what's happening to my people in Egypt. I heard they cries from all this oppression. Yeah, I know exactly what they goin' through.'
3.9: 'So I'm steppin' in to rescue 'em from Egypt and bring 'em to their own land—a land rich and full, flowin' with milk and honey. The same land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live now.'
3.10: 'Listen up, the cries of my people have reached me, and I see how bad the Egyptians treat 'em. So now, I'm sendin' you, Moses, to Pharaoh. You gon' lead my people, Israel, outta Egypt.'
3.11: But Moses was like, 'Wait, who am I to be standin' in front of Pharaoh? Who am I to be leadin' Israel outta Egypt?'
3.12: God told him, 'Don't even trip—I'ma be right there with you. And here's how you'll know I'm the one sendin' you: When you bring my people outta Egypt, y'all gon' worship me right here on this mountain.'
3.13: Moses said, 'Alright, but if I go tell the Israelites, "The God of your ancestors sent me," they gon' ask me, "What's His name?" What should I tell 'em?'
3.14: God said, 'Tell 'em this—"I Am Who I Am." That's what you tell the Israelites: "I Am sent me to you."'
3.15: Then God added, 'Tell 'em this too: "Yahweh, the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—sent me to you. This my name forever. This the name y'all gon' remember for all generations."'
3.16: 'Now go, gather all the elders of Israel and tell 'em, "Yahweh, the God of our ancestors—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—showed up to me. He told me He's been watching and He knows exactly how Egypt been treating us."'
3.17: 'Then tell 'em, "God promised He gon' rescue us from Egypt and take us to a land flowing with milk and honey—the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites."'
3.18: 'The elders gon' listen to you. Then you and them need to go to the king of Egypt and tell him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, showed up to us. Let us take a three-day trip into the wilderness so we can worship Him and offer sacrifices."'
3.19: 'But listen, Pharaoh ain't lettin' y'all go easy. He ain't gon' budge unless a mighty hand forces him.'
3.20: 'So I'ma raise my hand, hit Egypt with all kinds of miracles and wonders. And after that? Pharaoh gon' have no choice but to let y'all go.'
3.21: 'And check this—I'ma make sure the Egyptians look at y'all with favor before y'all leave. They gon' give y'all gifts, so y'all won't walk out empty-handed.'
3.22: 'Every Hebrew woman gon' ask her Egyptian neighbor for silver, gold, and fine clothes. Y'all gon' put 'em on your sons and daughters—straight up taking back what was stolen. Y'all gon' walk out of Egypt with their wealth in hand.'

4.1: But Moses was still trippin'. He said, 'What if they don't believe me? What if they don't listen? What if they say, "The Lord ain't appear to you"?'
4.2: Then the Lord said, 'What's that in your hand?'
4.3: Moses looked and said, 'A shepherd's staff.'
4.4: 'Throw it on the ground,' the Lord said. Moses threw it down, and boom—it turned into a snake! Moses jumped back real quick.
4.5: Then the Lord said, 'Reach out and grab its tail.' Moses hesitated, then reached out and grabbed it, and just like that—it turned back into a staff in his hand.
4.6: 'Do this sign,' the Lord told him. 'Then they'll believe that the God of their ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—really sent you.'
4.7: Then the Lord said, 'Now, put your hand inside your cloak.' So Moses did it, and when he pulled it out, his hand was all messed up—white as snow, covered in disease.
4.8: 'Now put it back inside your cloak,' God said. Moses did, and when he pulled it out again, it was back to normal.
4.9: 'If they don't believe the first sign, they'll believe the second one. But if they still don't listen, take some water from the Nile, pour it out on dry ground, and watch it turn to blood.'
4.10: Moses started makin' excuses again, 'Lord, I ain't good with words. Never been. Even now, after You talkin' to me, I still get tongue-tied and trip over my words.'
4.11: The Lord said, 'Who made the mouth? Who decides if folks can talk or not, hear or not, see or not? Ain't it Me, the Lord?'
4.12: 'Now go! I'ma be with you while you speak, and I'ma tell you exactly what to say.'
4.13: But Moses still wasn't feelin' it. 'Lord, please! Just send somebody else!'
4.14: Now God was gettin' frustrated. 'Alright then, what about your brother Aaron? He speaks well. Look, he already on his way to meet you, and he gon' be happy to see you.'
4.15: 'You gon' tell him what to say, and I'ma be with both of y'all as you speak. I'ma teach you exactly what to do.'
4.16: 'Aaron gon' be your spokesman to the people. He gon' speak for you, and you gon' be like a representative of God to him, tellin' him what to say.'
4.17: 'And don't forget that staff—take it with you, 'cause you gon' need it to perform these miracles.'
4.18: Moses went back home to his father-in-law, Jethro, and said, 'Let me go back to Egypt to check on my people. I don't even know if they still alive.'
4.20: Before Moses left Midian, the Lord spoke to him again: 'Go back to Egypt. The folks that wanted you dead? They all gone now.'
4.21: So Moses packed up, put his wife and kids on a donkey, and started heading to Egypt. In his hand? That staff of God.
4.22: Then the Lord told Moses, 'When you get back to Egypt, go to Pharaoh and do all the miracles I gave you power to do. But listen—he ain't gon' listen, 'cause I'ma make his heart stubborn.'
4.23: 'Then you tell him, "This is what the Lord says: Israel is my firstborn son. I told you, 'Let my son go, so he can worship me.' But since you refused, now I'ma take your firstborn son."'
4.24: While Moses and his family were stopped for the night, the Lord rolled up on him, ready to take him out.
4.25: But Zipporah, his wife, grabbed a flint knife, circumcised their son on the spot, and touched Moses' feet with the skin. She said, 'Now you a bridegroom of blood to me.'
4.26: (She was talkin' 'bout circumcision.) After that, the Lord backed off and left Moses alone.
4.27: Meanwhile, the Lord told Aaron, 'Go meet your brother in the wilderness.' So Aaron went and met Moses at the mountain of God, and they hugged it out.
4.28: Moses told Aaron everything the Lord said and showed him all the miracles they had to perform.
4.29: Then Moses and Aaron went back to Egypt and called all the elders of Israel together.
4.30: Aaron told them everything the Lord told Moses, and Moses performed the miracles right in front of them.
4.31: The people believed! And when they heard the Lord had seen their struggle and was about to free them, they bowed down and worshiped.

5.1: After Moses and Aaron spoke with Israel's leaders, they went to Pharaoh and said, 'This what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Let my people go so they can hold a festival for me in the wilderness.'
5.2: Pharaoh snapped back, 'Oh, for real? And who this Lord y'all talkin' about? Why should I listen to Him and let Israel go? I don't know no Lord, and I ain't lettin' Israel go nowhere.'
5.3: But Moses and Aaron stood their ground, 'The God of the Hebrews met with us. We need to take a three-day trip into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to Him. If we don't, He gon' send a plague or bring the sword down on us.'
5.4: Pharaoh shook his head, 'Moses, Aaron, why y'all out here distracting these people from their work? Get back to it!'
5.5: 'Look, there's too many of y'all in this land, and now you tryna slow 'em down? Nah, get back to work!'
5.6: That same day, Pharaoh gave an order to the Egyptian slave drivers and the Israelite foremen.
5.7: 'Aye, stop givin' them straw for their bricks. Make 'em go get it theyself!'
5.8: 'But don't let up on the number of bricks they gotta make. Keep the quota the same. These folks lazy. That's why they out here talkin' 'bout, "Let us go worship our God."'
5.9: 'Make 'em work harder! Load 'em up till they too tired to listen to them lies.'
5.10: So the slave drivers and foremen went out and told the people, 'This what Pharaoh says: Y'all ain't gettin' no more straw.'
5.11: 'Go find it yourselves wherever you can, but you still gotta make the same amount of bricks!'
5.12: So the people scattered all over Egypt, tryna find anything they could use instead of straw.
5.13: Meanwhile, the Egyptian slave drivers kept pressing 'em, 'Y'all better hit that daily brick quota just like before, even without straw!'
5.14: Then they started beating the Israelite foremen they put in charge of the work crews. 'Why y'all ain't hit your brick numbers yesterday or today?!'
5.15: So the Israelite foremen went straight to Pharaoh and begged him, 'Please, don't treat us like this!'
5.16: 'We ain't gettin' no straw, but they still tellin' us, "Make bricks!" We gettin' beat, but this ain't even on us! Your own people the ones messin' up!'
5.17: But Pharaoh snapped, 'Nah, y'all just lazy! Lazy! That's why y'all keep askin' to go worship the Lord.'
5.18: 'Now get back to work! Ain't no straw comin', but y'all still gotta hit that full quota!'
5.19: The Israelite foremen walked outta there knowin' they was in serious trouble after Pharaoh told 'em, 'Don't reduce the number of bricks.'
5.20: As soon as they left Pharaoh's court, they ran into Moses and Aaron, who were waitin' outside.
5.21: They told them, 'Man, may the Lord judge y'all for this! Y'all done made us look bad in front of Pharaoh and his crew. Now they got a reason to kill us!'
5.22: Then Moses went back to the Lord and said, 'Lord, why You let this happen to Your people? Why You even send me?'
5.23: 'Ever since I went to Pharaoh like You told me, he been even more brutal to Your people. And You ain't done nothin' to rescue 'em!'

6.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, now you about to see what I'ma do to Pharaoh. When he feel the power of My strong hand, he gon' let y'all go. Matter fact, he gon' be the one forcing y'all to leave!'
6.2: Then God said to Moses, 'I am Yahweh—the Lord.'
6.3: 'I showed up to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El-Shaddai—God Almighty—but I ain't reveal My name, Yahweh, to them.'
6.4: 'I made a covenant with them, and under that agreement, I promised to give them the land of Canaan, where they was living as foreigners.'
6.5: 'Best believe, I done heard the cries of My people in Egypt. They groanin' under slavery, and trust—I ain't forgot My promise to them.'
6.6: 'So tell Israel this: I am the Lord. I'ma free y'all from oppression, rescue y'all from slavery, and redeem y'all with My powerful hand and great acts of judgment.'
6.7: 'I'ma make y'all My people, and I'ma be your God. Then y'all gon' know that I am the Lord, y'all's God, the One who freed y'all from Egyptian oppression.'
6.8: 'I'ma bring y'all into the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I'ma give it to y'all as y'all own inheritance. I am the Lord!'
6.9: Moses went and told the Israelites what the Lord said, but they ain't even wanna hear it no more. They was too broke down from all the suffering and harsh slavery.
6.11: 'Go back to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and tell him to let My people leave his land.'
6.12: But Moses said, 'Lord, even my own people won't listen to me no more. How I'm supposed to make Pharaoh listen? I ain't even good at talkin'!'
6.13: But the Lord ain't let Moses off the hook. He gave orders to both Moses and Aaron about how they was gon' lead Israel outta Egypt, and what to say to Pharaoh.
6.14: Here go some of the ancestors of Israel's clans: Reuben, Israel's oldest son, had sons—Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. Their descendants became the clans of Reuben.
6.15: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul (whose mama was a Canaanite). Their descendants became the clans of Simeon.
6.16: These the descendants of Levi, written down in their family records: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
6.17: The descendants of Gershon included Libni and Shimei, and their clans.
6.18: The descendants of Kohath included Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
6.19: The descendants of Merari included Mahli and Mushi. These was the Levite clans, listed in their family records.
6.20: Amram married his aunt Jochebed, and they had two sons—Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.
6.21: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zicri.
6.22: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
6.23: Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon. They had sons—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
6.24: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. Their descendants became the clans of Korah.
6.25: Eleazar, son of Aaron, married a daughter of Putiel, and they had a son named Phinehas. These were the ancestors of the Levite families, listed by clans.
6.26: This Aaron and Moses in the list are the same ones the Lord told, 'Lead My people out of Egypt like an army.'
6.27: They the same ones who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, about bringing Israel outta slavery.
6.28: When the Lord spoke to Moses in Egypt,
6.29: He told him, 'I am the Lord! Go tell Pharaoh everything I tell you.'
6.30: But Moses argued back, 'Lord, I can't do this! I don't talk right! Why would Pharaoh even listen to me?'

7.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Listen up. I'ma make you seem like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron gon' be your prophet.'
7.2: 'You tell Aaron everything I command you, and he gon' tell Pharaoh to let My people go.'
7.3: 'But I'ma make Pharaoh's heart stubborn so I can drop all My miracles and wonders across Egypt.'
7.4: 'Even then, Pharaoh ain't gon' listen. So I'ma hit Egypt hard. Then I'ma step in, bring My people—Israel—outta Egypt with serious judgment.'
7.5: 'And when I flex My power and bring Israel out, Egypt gon' know exactly who I am—the Lord.'
7.6: So Moses and Aaron did exactly what the Lord told 'em to do.
7.7: Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron was 83 when they rolled up on Pharaoh.
7.8: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,
7.9: 'Pharaoh gon' ask y'all to prove yourselves with a miracle. When he does, tell Aaron to throw his staff down in front of Pharaoh—it's gon' turn into a snake.'
7.10: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did exactly what the Lord said. Aaron threw down his staff in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and—boom!—it turned into a snake!
7.11: Then Pharaoh called up his wise men, sorcerers, and magicians, and they did the same thing using their magic.
7.12: They threw down their staffs, and they turned into snakes too! But then Aaron's staff ate up all their staffs.
7.13: Still, Pharaoh wasn't fazed. His heart stayed hard, and just like the Lord said, he ain't listen.
7.14: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Pharaoh still got his heart locked up—he ain't tryna let the people go.'
7.15: 'So tomorrow morning, go meet him at the Nile River when he goin' down there. Take that staff that turned into a snake with you.'
7.16: 'Then tell him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to tell you: Let My people go so they can worship Me in the wilderness. But you ain't listen."'
7.17: 'So now, this what the Lord says: "I'ma show you who I am. Watch—I'ma strike the Nile with this staff, and the whole river gon' turn to blood."'
7.18: 'The fish in it gon' die, the river gon' stink, and the Egyptians ain't gon' be able to drink from it.'
7.19: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to lift up his staff and stretch it over all the waters of Egypt—the rivers, canals, ponds, and reservoirs. Turn all of it to blood, even the water sittin' in wooden bowls and stone pots.'
7.20: So Moses and Aaron did just what the Lord commanded. While Pharaoh and his officials watched, Aaron raised his staff and hit the Nile—and just like that, the whole river turned to blood!
7.21: The fish died, the river stank, and the Egyptians couldn't drink from it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
7.22: But Pharaoh's magicians did the same thing with their tricks, so Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. He refused to listen to Moses and Aaron, just like the Lord had said.
7.23: Pharaoh just went back to his palace like it was nothin'. Didn't even let it bother him.
7.24: Meanwhile, the Egyptians had to start digging along the riverbank just to find drinking water, 'cause the Nile was useless.
7.25: This plague lasted a whole seven days from when the Lord hit the Nile.

8.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Go back to Pharaoh and tell him, "This what the Lord says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'
8.2: 'If you don't, I'ma send a plague of frogs all over your land.'
8.3: 'The Nile gon' be crawling with frogs—they comin' up out the river into your palace, your bedroom, even on your bed! They gon' be in your officials' houses, your people's houses, even hoppin' in y'all's ovens and kneading bowls.'
8.4: 'Frogs gon' be all over you, your people, and your officials—ain't no escaping 'em.'
8.5: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to raise his staff over all the waters of Egypt—rivers, canals, and ponds—and bring up frogs all over the land.'
8.6: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and just like that—frogs swarmed everywhere, covering Egypt!
8.7: But Pharaoh's magicians pulled the same trick with their magic—they brought up more frogs too!
8.8: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, beggin', 'Yo, ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people! If you do, I'ma let y'all go worship the Lord.'
8.9: Moses said, 'Alright, you tell me when you want me to pray for you, your officials, and your people so the frogs bounce out and stay only in the Nile.'
8.10: 'Tomorrow,' Pharaoh said. Moses replied, 'Bet. Just like you said. Then you'll know ain't nobody like the Lord our God.'
8.11: 'The frogs gon' be gone from you, your houses, your officials, and your people. They only gon' stay in the Nile.'
8.12: So Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh's palace, and Moses cried out to the Lord about the frogs.
8.13: And the Lord did exactly what Moses asked—frogs in the houses, courtyards, and fields all dropped dead.
8.14: The Egyptians piled 'em up into big ol' heaps, and the whole land started smelling rank.
8.15: But soon as Pharaoh saw relief, he went right back to being stubborn. He ain't listen to Moses and Aaron, just like the Lord said he wouldn't.
8.16: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to raise his staff and strike the ground—the dust gon' turn into gnats all over Egypt.'
8.17: So Moses and Aaron did exactly what the Lord said. Aaron hit the ground with his staff, and boom—gnats swarmed the whole land, coverin' up the Egyptians and their animals. The dust all over Egypt turned into gnats.
8.18: Pharaoh's magicians tried to pull the same move, but this time they failed. Gnats was all over everybody—people and animals alike.
8.19: The magicians went to Pharaoh and said, 'Yo, this the finger of God!' But Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. He still wouldn't listen, just like the Lord predicted.
8.20: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Get up early and go block Pharaoh when he head to the river. Tell him, "This what the Lord says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'
8.21: 'If you don't, I'ma send swarms of flies all over you, your officials, your people, and your houses. The whole land gon' be crawling with flies.'
8.22: 'But this time, I'ma do something different—I'ma spare Goshen, where My people live. No flies gon' be there. Then you'll know I'm the Lord, right here in the middle of Egypt.'
8.23: 'I'ma make it real clear—there's a difference between My people and yours. This miracle happenin' tomorrow.'
8.24: And the Lord did just that. Swarms of flies flooded Pharaoh's palace, his officials' houses—flies everywhere. The whole land of Egypt was straight-up chaotic.
8.25: Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, 'Aight! Go ahead and sacrifice to your God—but do it here in Egypt.'
8.26: Moses said, 'Nah, that ain't gon' work. The Egyptians don't mess with the sacrifices we make to the Lord. If we do that here where they can see us, they gon' stone us!'
8.27: 'We need to take a three-day trip into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord, just like He told us to.'
8.28: Pharaoh said, 'Aight, fine. Y'all can go sacrifice in the wilderness, just don't go too far. But hurry up and pray for me.'
8.29: Moses said, 'Aight, soon as I leave, I'ma pray to the Lord, and by tomorrow all the flies gon' be gone from you, your officials, and your people. But Pharaoh, I'm warning you—don't play us again and refuse to let us go worship the Lord.'
8.30: So Moses left Pharaoh's palace and prayed to the Lord.
8.31: And the Lord did exactly what Moses asked—every last fly disappeared from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not a single one left.
8.32: But guess what? Pharaoh turned stubborn again. He refused to let the people go.

9.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Go back to Pharaoh and tell him, "This what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'
9.2: 'If you keep holdin' on to them and won't let 'em go…'
9.3: 'Then My hand gon' strike all your livestock—your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep, and goats—with a deadly plague.'
9.4: 'But I'ma make sure there's a difference between Israel's animals and Egypt's animals. Not a single one of theirs gon' die!'
9.5: 'The Lord already set the time—tomorrow, this plague comin' down on Egypt.'
9.6: And just like that, the next morning, all the Egyptian livestock died—but not a single Israelite animal was lost.
9.7: Pharaoh sent his officials to check, and sure enough, not one of Israel's animals was dead! But Pharaoh? He still kept his heart hard and wouldn't let the people go.

16.19: Then Moses told 'em, 'Don't keep none till the mornin'!'
16.20: But some ain't listen—tried to keep some overnight. By mornin'? It was full of maggots & stinkin'. Moses was big mad.
16.21: So from then on, they gathered it every morning, just what they needed. But when the sun got hot, anything left on the ground melted away.
16.22: On the sixth day, they picked up twice as much—four quarts per person. All the leaders came to Moses like, 'Yo, what's this about?'
16.23: Moses told 'em, 'This what the Lord say—Tomorrow's the Sabbath. Ain't no food comin', so cook what you need today and set the rest aside for tomorrow.'
16.24: So they put some up for later—and this time it ain't rot or stink.
16.25: Moses said, 'See? Eat it today. It's the Lord's Sabbath. Ain't gon' be nothin' on the ground today.'
16.26: 'Six days y'all can gather food, but on the seventh day, ain't gon' be nothin' there.'
16.27: Still, some of 'em tried to go out on the Sabbath to get food—they found nothin'.
16.28: Then the Lord was like, 'How long y'all gon' keep ignorin' what I say?'
16.29: 'Y'all need to understand—this Sabbath is My gift to y'all. That's why I gave y'all twice the food on the sixth day. Stay home! Ain't no need to go out on the seventh day.'
16.30: So the people finally got it and stayed home on the Sabbath.
16.31: The Israelites called the food manna. It was white, lookin' like coriander seeds, and it tasted like honey biscuits.
16.32: Moses said, 'The Lord want y'all to keep some of this, so later generations can see the food He gave us when He brought us outta Egypt.'
16.33: Then Moses told Aaron, 'Take a jar, fill it with two quarts of manna, and keep it in a sacred place before the Lord.'
16.34: So Aaron did just that. Eventually, he put it in the Ark of the Covenant, right in front of the stone tablets of God's law.
16.35: The Israelites ate manna for 40 years, until they reached the land of Canaan.
16.36: The measurement they used—an omer—was about two quarts.

17.1: The whole Israelite crew followed the Lord's command, movin' from spot to spot through the wilderness of Sin. Eventually, they camped at Rephidim, but ain't no water out there to drink.
17.2: So, like always, the people started pressin' Moses again. 'We need water! Give us somethin' to drink!' they demanded. Moses snapped back, 'Man, calm down! Why y'all always fussin' at me? And why y'all keep testin' the Lord?'
17.3: But these folks was mad thirsty, so they kept arguin' with Moses. 'Man, why you even bring us outta Egypt? Tryin' to kill us, our kids, and all our animals with thirst?!'
17.4: So Moses straight up cried out to the Lord, 'What am I supposed to do with these people?! They 'bout ready to stone me!'
17.5: The Lord said, 'Aight, here's what you gon' do—step up in front of everybody, take that staff you used when you struck the Nile, and grab some of the elders to roll with you.'
17.6: 'I'ma be right there standin' on the rock at Mount Sinai. You gon' hit that rock, and water gon' come bustin' out so everybody can drink.' Moses did exactly what the Lord said, and water came gushin' out while the elders watched.
17.7: Moses named that place Massah (which means 'test') and Meribah (which means 'arguin'')—'cause the Israelites stayed arguin' with Moses and testin' the Lord, askin', 'Is God even here with us or not?'
17.8: While the Israelites was still at Rephidim, the Amalekites rolled up and attacked them.
17.9: Moses told Joshua, 'Pick some dudes to roll out and fight Amalek for us. Tomorrow, I'ma be up on the hill holdin' the staff of God.'
17.10: So Joshua did what Moses said and got his squad ready to fight. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed up on a hill.
17.11: Check this—as long as Moses held up his staff, the Israelites was doin' good. But whenever he dropped his hands, the Amalekites started winnin' the fight.
17.12: Moses' arms got tired, and he couldn't hold 'em up no more. So Aaron and Hur grabbed a stone for him to sit on, then they held up his arms, one on each side. His hands stayed steady all the way till sunset.
17.13: Joshua and his squad straight up crushed the Amalekites in battle.
17.14: After the fight, the Lord told Moses, 'Write this down so folks don't forget. Read it to Joshua—I'ma erase the memory of Amalek from the earth.'
17.15: Moses built an altar and called it Yahweh-Nissi (which means 'The Lord is my banner').
17.16: Then he said, 'These folks came for the Lord's people, so now God gon' be at war with Amalek forever.'

18.1: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, who was the priest of Midian, heard all 'bout what God had done for Moses and the Israelites. Especially how the Lord brought 'em up outta Egypt.
18.2: Moses had sent his wife, Zipporah, and his two sons back to Jethro, and Jethro had been lookin' after them.
18.3: (Moses' first son was Gershom, 'cause Moses said, 'I been a foreigner in a land that ain't mine.'
18.4: His second son was Eliezer, 'cause Moses said, 'The God of my ancestors had my back and saved me from Pharaoh's sword.')
18.5: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to visit Moses out in the wilderness, bringing Zipporah and the two boys with him. They pulled up near the mountain of God.
18.6: Jethro sent Moses a message: 'Yo, I'm on my way to see you. I got your wife and kids with me.'
18.7: Moses went out to meet him, bowed low, and gave him a kiss of respect. They chopped it up, asked how each other was doing, then went into Moses' tent.
18.8: Moses broke it all down for Jethro—how the Lord took down Pharaoh, how He came through for Israel, and all the hardships they faced on the way. He told him how the Lord kept rescuing them.
18.9: Jethro was hyped when he heard all the good things the Lord had done for Israel, especially how He saved them from Egypt.
18.10: Jethro said, 'Praise the Lord! He really came through for y'all, snatchin' y'all outta Pharaoh's grip and outta Egypt's control.'
18.11: 'Now I know for sure that the Lord is the realest—greater than any other god! He put Egypt in check for all that oppression they was on.'
18.12: Then Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and the elders of Israel came through and joined him for a sacrificial meal in God's presence.
18.13: The next day, Moses sat down to judge the people's problems. From morning 'til evening, folks lined up waiting on him.
18.14: When Jethro saw what was goin' down, he was like, 'Bruh, what is you doin'?! Why you tryna handle all this alone while everybody just stand around all day?'
18.15: Moses said, 'They come to me to get a ruling from God.'
18.16: 'Whenever folks got beef, they come to me. I settle it, tell 'em what God says, and teach 'em His laws and ways.'
18.18: 'You gon' burn out, and the people too! This is way too much for one man to handle.'
18.19: 'Listen to me, I'ma put you on game—and may God be with you. You still gon' represent the people before God and bring their problems to Him.
18.20: 'Teach them God's laws, show them the way to live, and how to do right.'
18.21: 'But here's what you gotta do—pick out some solid men. Get some capable, honest dudes who fear God and don't take bribes. Put 'em over groups of 1,000, 100, 50, and 10.'
18.22: 'Let them handle the everyday disputes, but the big cases come to you. That way, you ain't doin' all the heavy liftin' alone.'
18.23: 'If you do this, and God cosigns it, you gon' last longer, and the people gon' be straight.'
18.24: Moses listened to Jethro's advice and put the plan in motion.
18.25: He picked out capable men, put 'em over groups, and made 'em leaders.
18.26: They started handling disputes on the daily, only bringing the serious ones to Moses.
18.27: After all that, Moses said goodbye to his father-in-law, and Jethro headed back home.

19.1: Two months after leavin' Egypt, the Israelites pulled up in the Sinai wilderness.
19.2: They left Rephidim, moved through the desert, and set up camp at the foot of Mount Sinai.
19.3: Moses climbed up the mountain to meet God. The Lord called out, 'Moses, tell the people of Israel this:'
19.4: 'Y'all saw what I did to the Egyptians. I carried y'all like eagles and brought you straight to me.'
19.5: 'Now, if y'all listen to me and keep this agreement, y'all gon' be my special treasure—set apart from every other nation. Everything in the world is mine, but y'all different.'
19.6: 'Y'all gon' be a kingdom of priests, a holy nation. That's what you tell Israel.'
19.7: Moses came down, gathered the elders, and told 'em what God said.
19.8: The people all said, 'We down for whatever the Lord says.' So Moses went back and told the Lord their answer.
19.9: Then the Lord told Moses, 'I'ma pull up in a thick cloud so the people can hear me talk to you. That way, they'll always trust what you say.'
19.10: Then the Lord said, 'Go prep the people. Get 'em clean today and tomorrow—have 'em wash their clothes.'
19.11: 'Tell 'em to be ready on the third day, 'cause that's when I'ma show up on Mount Sinai.'
19.12: 'Mark off a boundary around the mountain. Tell the people, "Don't cross this line! Don't even touch the mountain!" Anybody who does gon' die.'
19.13: 'Don't let nobody touch them—stone 'em or shoot 'em with arrows. But when y'all hear the ram's horn blow long, that's the cue—then folks can come up.'
19.14: So Moses went down, told the people to get right, and they washed their clothes.
19.15: He told them, 'Get ready for the third day, and don't be messin' around with your spouses until then.'
19.16: Early on the third day, thunder shook the sky, lightning flashed, and a thick cloud covered the mountain. A loud ram's horn blasted, and the people started trembling.
19.17: Moses led the people out the camp to meet God, and they stood at the base of Mount Sinai.
19.18: The whole mountain was covered in smoke 'cause the Lord came down in fire. The smoke shot up like from a brick oven, and the whole mountain was shakin'.
19.19: The ram's horn kept blasting louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered in thunder.
19.20: The Lord came down on top of Sinai and called Moses up. So Moses climbed up.
19.21: The Lord said, 'Go back down and warn the people—tell 'em not to try and sneak up to see me, or they gon' die.'
19.22: 'Even the priests that come close need to clean themselves up first. Otherwise, I'ma handle them too.'
19.23: Moses was like, 'Lord, we already set the boundary. You told me to mark off the mountain as holy.'
19.24: But the Lord said, 'Go get Aaron and bring him back up. But nobody else, not even the priests, better try to come up here, or they gon' be done for.'
19.25: So Moses went down, told the people exactly what God said.

20.1: Then God spoke up and gave 'em these rules:
20.2: 'I'm the Lord your God, the one who broke y'all outta Egypt, took y'all outta slavery.'
20.3: 'Ain't nobody else supposed to be your god but me.'
20.4: 'Don't be out here makin' idols, statues, or images of anything in the sky, on earth, or in the sea. None of that.'
20.5: 'Don't bow down to them or worship them 'cause I'm a jealous God. I ain't toleratin' y'all cheatin' on me with other gods. Mess up, and it ain't just you—it's gon' hit your kids too, all the way down to the third and fourth generation if y'all reject me.'
20.6: 'But stay loyal to me, follow my commands, and I'll bless a thousand generations of your people.'
20.7: 'Don't play with my name. Don't be out here uselessly swearin' on me. I ain't lettin' that slide.'
20.9: 'Y'all got six days to handle business, to do all your regular work.'
20.10: 'But the seventh day? That's my day. No work. That goes for you, your kids, your workers, your animals— even the foreigners in your land.'
20.11: 'I made everything in six days—the sky, the earth, the sea—and I rested on the seventh. So I blessed the Sabbath and made it special.'
20.12: 'Honor your mama and daddy so you can live long in the land I'm givin' you.'
20.17: 'Don't be jealous of your neighbor's stuff—not their house, not their spouse, not their workers, not their animals— don't lust after nothin' that ain't yours.'
20.18: When the people saw the lightning, heard the thunder, and the loud blast of the ram's horn, and saw the smoke on the mountain, they were shook. They stood back, trembling.
20.19: They told Moses, 'You talk to us, we'll listen. But we ain't tryin' to hear from God directly, we gon' die if we do!'
20.20: Moses told 'em, 'Y'all chill. Don't be scared. God just came to test y'all so y'all respect him enough not to sin.'
20.21: While the people kept their distance, Moses stepped into the thick cloud where God was.
20.22: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, 'Tell the people—Y'all saw me speak from heaven.'
20.23: 'So don't even think about makin' idols, not gold, not silver, nothin' to compete with me. I ain't sharing my shine.'
20.24: 'Build an altar from the ground, offer your sacrifices—burnt offerings, peace offerings, your sheep, goats, and cattle. Build it where I make my name known, and I'ma bless you.'
20.25: 'If you use stones for my altar, don't cut 'em with tools—that messes it up.'
20.26: 'And don't build no steps to my altar. We ain't tryna have nobody peepin' up under your robe.'

21.1: 'These the rules you gotta tell Israel.'
21.2: 'If you buy a Hebrew servant, he only workin' six years. On year seven, let 'em go free—he ain't gotta pay nothin' for it.'
21.3: 'If he came in single, he leave single. If he got a wife, she walkin' free with him.'
21.4: 'Now, if his master gave him a wife, and they had kids, then only he gets free. The wife and kids still belong to the master.'
21.5: 'But if the servant say, 'I love my master, my wife, and my kids—I ain't tryin' to leave,'
21.6: 'Then his master gotta take him before God. Then he gotta pierce his ear against the doorpost, and from then on, that man servin' for life.'
21.7: 'If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she ain't leavin' in year seven like the men do.'
21.8: 'If she don't please the master who bought her, he gotta let her be bought back. But he can't sell her to foreigners—that's foul since he already broke the deal.'
21.9: 'If the master set her up to marry his son, he gotta treat her like a daughter.'
21.10: 'If he marry her then take another wife, he still gotta give her food, clothes, and love.'
21.11: 'If he don't do those three things, she walkin' free, no payment needed.'
21.12: 'Anybody that kills somebody on purpose? They gotta die too.'
21.13: 'But if it was an accident, then I'ma make a safe place for 'em to run to.'
21.14: 'Now, if somebody planned it out, they gon' die—don't matter if they run to my altar or not.'
21.15: 'If somebody hit their mama or daddy, they gotta die.'
21.16: 'Kidnappers? If they caught with the victim, or if they already sold them, they gon' die too.'
21.17: 'If you curse ya mama or daddy, guess what? Death.'
21.18: 'If two men get into it, and one hit the other with a rock or a fist, but he don't die—'
21.19: 'If he get better later and can walk again, even with a cane, the dude that hit him ain't gettin' punished—but he gotta pay for them lost wages till the man get back on his feet.'
21.20: 'If a master beat his servant and they die on the spot, that master gotta be punished.'
21.21: 'But if the servant recover after a day or two, the master ain't gettin' punished—that's still his property.'
21.22: 'If two men fightin', and they accidentally hit a pregnant woman so she gives birth too soon—if the baby ain't hurt, the man payin' whatever the husband demand.'
21.23: 'But if somebody die, then it's life for life.'
21.24: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.'
21.25: 'Burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.'
21.26: 'If a master hit a servant and they lose an eye, that servant gotta be freed as payback.'
21.27: 'If a master knock out a tooth, the servant walkin' free as compensation.'
21.28: 'If an ox kills somebody, that ox gotta be stoned, and nobody eatin' the meat. But the owner ain't responsible.'
21.29: 'BUT, if that ox was known for wildin', and the owner didn't stop it—and it killed somebody, then both the ox and the owner gotta die.'
21.30: 'Unless the victim's family wanna take money instead, then the owner can buy his life back.'
21.31: 'Same rule apply if it kills a kid.'
21.32: 'If an ox kills a slave, the owner gotta pay thirty silver coins to the slave's master, and the ox still gets stoned.'
21.33: 'If somebody digs a pit and leaves it uncovered, and an ox or donkey falls in—'
21.34: 'Then the pit owner gotta pay the animal's owner, but they keep the dead animal.'
21.35: 'If one person's ox kills another person's ox, then they gotta sell the live one and split the money, and they split the dead animal too.'
21.36: 'But if the ox was known for goring, and the owner ain't stop it, then he payin' full price, but he keeps the dead ox.'

22.1: 'If somebody steal an ox or a sheep, then kill it or sell it, that thief gotta pay back five oxen for every ox they took, and four sheep for every sheep they stole.'
22.2: 'If a thief break into a house at night and get killed, the one who killed 'em ain't guilty of murder.'
22.3: 'But if it happen in daylight, then the one who killed 'em guilty of murder. If the thief get caught, they gotta pay back what they stole. If they ain't got the money, they gon' be sold as a servant to pay it off.'
22.4: 'If somebody steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and they still got it, then they payin' back double.'
22.5: 'If somebody's animal wander into another man's field and start eatin' up crops, the owner of the animal gotta pay up with the best of their own crops.'
22.6: 'If you burnin' bushes and the fire get loose and burn somebody's crops, the one who started it gotta pay for all the damage.'
22.7: 'If somebody leave money or goods with a neighbor for safekeeping, and it get stolen, if the thief get caught, they payin' back double.'
22.8: 'But if the thief ain't caught, the neighbor gotta go before God, and God gon' judge if they guilty or not.'
22.9: 'If two people arguin' over who own somethin'—like an ox, donkey, or clothes—God gon' decide who guilty. Whoever wrong gotta pay back double.'
22.10: 'If somebody leave an animal with a neighbor and it die or disappear, and nobody saw what happened—'
22.11: 'Then the neighbor gotta swear before God they ain't steal it. If they ain't guilty, no payment required.'
22.12: 'But if it was stolen, then the neighbor gotta pay back the owner.'
22.13: 'If a wild animal killed it, then they just gotta show proof—they ain't gotta pay nothin'.'
22.14: 'If somebody borrow an animal, and it die or get hurt while the owner ain't around, they gotta pay for it.'
22.15: 'But if the owner was there, they ain't gotta pay. If the animal was rented, the rental fee covers the loss.'
22.16: 'If a man sleep with a virgin that ain't engaged, he gotta marry her and pay the bride price.'
22.17: 'If her daddy say no, the man still gotta pay like he would if he was marryin' her.'
22.19: 'Anybody lay with an animal? They dyin'.'
22.20: 'Anybody worship another god other than the Lord? They gon' be destroyed.'
22.21: 'Don't mistreat foreigners. Remember, y'all was foreigners in Egypt. Treat them right.'
22.23: 'If you do 'em wrong and they cry out to Me, I will hear 'em.'
22.24: 'And if I hear 'em cry, my anger gon' blaze, and I'ma kill you with the sword. Then yo' wives gon' be widows and yo' kids gon' be orphans.'
22.25: 'If you lend money to somebody broke, don't charge interest like a loan shark.'
22.26: 'If you take somebody's coat as security for a loan, give it back before the sun set.'
22.27: 'That's the only blanket they got—how they gon' sleep without it? If they cry to Me, I will hear, 'cause I'm merciful.'
22.28: 'Don't dishonor God or curse your leaders.'
22.29: 'When you give me offerings, don't hold back from the first of your harvest and wine.'
22.31: 'Y'all belong to Me, so don't eat no animal that been torn up by wild beasts—throw that to the dogs.'

23.1: 'Don't be spreadin' no false rumors, and don't team up with evil folks to lie in court.'
23.2: 'Don't just go along with the crowd when they doin' wrong. If you called to testify, don't twist the truth just 'cause everybody else sayin' somethin' different.'
23.3: 'And don't change up your story just 'cause somebody poor—tell the truth, no matter what.'
23.4: 'If you see your enemy's ox or donkey that ran off, take it back to 'em.'
23.5: 'If you see somebody you don't like strugglin' 'cause their donkey collapsed, don't just keep it pushin'—help 'em out.'
23.6: 'In court, don't cheat a poor person out of justice. Fair is fair.'
23.7: 'Don't accuse nobody falsely or sentence an innocent person to death, 'cause I don't clear guilty folks.'
23.8: 'Don't take no bribes, 'cause that money will make you blind to the truth and mess up even an honest person's judgment.'
23.9: 'Don't be out here oppressin' foreigners. Y'all know what it's like to be foreigners, 'cause y'all was foreigners in Egypt. Treat them right.'
23.10: 'Work your land for six years, grow your crops and harvest 'em—'
23.11: 'But on the seventh year, let the land rest so the poor folks can get what they need, and whatever's left, let the wild animals have it.'
23.12: 'Y'all work six days a week, but on the seventh day, y'all rest—that way, yo' ox and donkey get a break, and so do yo' workers and foreigners.'
23.13: 'Listen real close to everything I'm tellin' y'all—don't call on no other gods, don't even say their names.'
23.14: 'Y'all gotta celebrate three festivals for Me every year.'
23.15: 'First, celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread with no yeast, just like I told y'all. This happen every spring, the same time y'all left Egypt. Don't come to Me empty-handed.'
23.16: 'Second, celebrate the Festival of Harvest—that's when you bring Me the first of what you grew.'
23.17: 'Then, celebrate the Final Harvest Festival at the end of the season when you gather everything up. Three times a year, every man in Israel gotta show up before the Lord.'
23.18: 'Don't offer sacrifices with bread that got yeast in it, and don't leave no fat from the festival offerings overnight. Clean it up.'
23.19: 'When y'all harvest crops, bring the best of what you got to the house of the Lord. And don't be cookin' no young goat in its mama's milk.'
23.20: 'Look, I'm sendin' an angel ahead of y'all to keep y'all safe on the journey and bring y'all to the place I promised.'
23.21: 'Listen up—do what he say and don't go against him. He ain't gon' tolerate y'all actin' up, 'cause he reppin' Me.'
23.22: 'But if y'all listen to him and do what I say, I'll be against anybody that's against you. I got y'all.'
23.23: 'My angel gon' lead y'all to the land where the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites live. I'ma wipe them out.'
23.24: 'But don't mess with their gods, don't worship 'em, don't copy their ways—y'all gotta destroy all that mess.'
23.25: 'Y'all serve Me, the Lord, and I'ma bless y'all with food and water, and I'ma keep y'all healthy.'
23.26: 'Nobody gon' miscarry or be infertile in the land, and I'ma make sure y'all live long full lives.'
23.27: 'I'ma send fear ahead of y'all—gonna make all these other folks panic before y'all even show up.'
23.28: 'I'ma run out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites before y'all even touch the land. They gon' clear out.'
23.29: 'But not too fast—if I run 'em out all at once, the land gon' be too empty, and wild animals gon' take over.'
23.30: 'I'ma push 'em out little by little till y'all got enough people to fill the land.'
23.31: 'Y'all boundaries gon' stretch from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I'ma hand them folks over to y'all, and y'all gon' drive 'em out.'
23.32: 'Don't make no treaties with them or their gods. No deals.'
23.33: 'Don't let 'em stay in yo' land, 'cause they gon' turn y'all away from Me. If y'all serve their gods, y'all gon' get caught up in idolatry, and it's gon' be a trap.'

24.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, come up here to Me, and bring Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel. But listen—y'all gotta worship from a distance.'
24.2: 'Only Moses can come close to Me. The rest of 'em? They gotta stay back. And nobody else better try climbin' this mountain.'
24.3: So Moses went down and told the people everything the Lord said—all the rules and commands. And the people, all together, said, 'We gon' do everything the Lord said. No cap!'
24.4: Then Moses wrote it all down. Early the next morning, he built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He also set up twelve stone pillars, one for each tribe of Israel.
24.5: Then he told some young Israelite men to offer burnt sacrifices and peace offerings—bulls for the Lord.
24.6: Moses took half the blood and put it in bowls. The other half? He splattered it on the altar.
24.7: Then he grabbed the Book of the Covenant and read it out loud to the people. Once again, they responded, 'We gon' do everything the Lord said. We gon' obey!'
24.8: Then Moses took the blood and splattered it over the people, sayin', 'Look, this blood seals the covenant the Lord made with y'all through these commands.'
24.9: Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel went up the mountain.
24.10: And they saw God—for real. Under His feet, there was somethin' like blue lapis lazuli—clear as the sky. Straight heavenly.
24.11: Even though they looked at God, He didn't strike 'em down. Matter fact, they sat there eatin' and drinkin' right in His presence!
24.12: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Come up higher. Stay here. I'ma give you stone tablets with all My commands, so you can teach the people.
24.13: So Moses and his assistant Joshua got ready, and Moses started climbin' up Mount Sinai.
24.14: Moses told the elders, 'Y'all wait here 'til we get back. If anybody got a problem while I'm gone, Aaron and Hur got this.'
24.15: Then Moses went up the mountain, and a thick cloud covered it.
24.16: The glory of the Lord came down on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, the Lord called Moses from inside the cloud.
24.17: From the Israelites' perspective, the glory of the Lord at the top of the mountain looked like a raging fire.
24.18: Then Moses walked into the cloud as he climbed higher up the mountain. He stayed up there for forty days and forty nights.

25.2: 'Tell the people of Israel to bring Me sacred offerings. Only take contributions from folks who really wanna give from the heart.
25.3: 'Here's what y'all can bring: Gold, silver, and bronze.
25.4: Blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goats' hair;
25.5: Ram skins dyed red, badger skins, and acacia wood;
25.6: Oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense;
25.7: Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod and in the breastplate.
25.8: Tell the people to build Me a holy sanctuary so I can stay with them.
25.9: Make sure the Tabernacle and everything in it is built exactly how I show you.
25.10: Tell the people to make an Ark outta acacia wood. It gotta be 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high.
25.11: Overlay it inside and out with pure gold and run a gold molding all around it.
25.12: Cast four gold rings and attach 'em to its feet—two rings on each side.
25.13: Make some poles outta acacia wood and cover 'em with gold.
25.14: Slide them poles into the rings so y'all can carry the Ark.
25.15: Do NOT take them poles out. Leave them in place.
25.16: Once it's done, put inside the Ark the stone tablets with the covenant terms I'ma give you.
25.17: Then make the Ark's cover—the mercy seat—outta pure gold. 45 inches long, 27 inches wide.
25.18: Make two cherubim outta hammered gold. Put 'em on both ends of the atonement cover.
25.19: Mold the cherubim onto the cover as one solid piece.
25.20: These cherubim gotta face each other and look down on the atonement cover. Their wings gotta spread over it, protectin' it.
25.21: Inside the Ark, put the stone tablets with the covenant terms I give you. Then put the atonement cover on top.
25.22: That's where I'll meet you—above the atonement cover, between the gold cherubim that hover over the Ark. From there, I'ma give you My instructions for the people.
25.23: Make a table outta acacia wood. 36 inches long, 18 inches wide, 27 inches high.
25.24: Overlay it with pure gold and run a gold molding around it.
25.25: Make a 3-inch border all around it and run a gold molding along the border.
25.26: Put four gold rings on the table, one at each corner by the legs.
25.27: Attach the rings near the border to hold the poles for carrying it.
25.28: Make the poles outta acacia wood, cover 'em with gold, so you can carry the table.
25.29: Make special containers outta pure gold—bowls, ladles, pitchers, and jars for pourin' out offerings.
25.30: Always keep the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me.
25.31: Make a lampstand outta pure hammered gold—one whole piece with the base, stem, cups, buds, and petals.
25.32: It should have six branches comin' out the sides—three on each side.
25.33: Each branch should have three lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.
25.34: The center stem should have four lamp cups, also shaped like almond blossoms.
25.35: Put an almond bud under each pair of branches where they extend from the stem.
25.36: The whole thing gotta be one solid piece of pure gold, hammered out.
25.37: Then make seven lamps for the stand, set 'em up so they shine forward.
25.38: Make the lamp snuffers and trays outta pure gold too.
25.39: You'll need 75 pounds of pure gold for the lampstand and all its accessories.
25.40: Follow every detail I showed you here on the mountain. No improvisin'!

26.1: Make the Tabernacle from ten curtains of finely woven linen. Decorate 'em with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, with skillfully embroidered cherubim.
26.2: Each curtain gotta be the same size—42 feet long and 6 feet wide.
26.3: Join five of 'em together to make one long curtain, then join the other five into a second long curtain.
26.4: Put loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in each set.
26.5: Fifty loops should go along the edge of one curtain, and another fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain.
26.6: Then make fifty gold clasps and use 'em to fasten the long curtains together. That way, the Tabernacle will be one solid piece.
26.7: Make eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as the tent covering for the Tabernacle.
26.8: Each curtain gotta be the same size—45 feet long and 6 feet wide.
26.9: Join five curtains together to make one long curtain, and do the same with the other six. Let three feet from the second set hang over the front of the sacred tent.
26.10: Make fifty loops on one edge of each large curtain.
26.11: Then make fifty bronze clasps, and fasten the loops together so the tent covering is one solid piece.
26.12: The extra three feet of the tent covering should hang over the back of the Tabernacle.
26.13: Eighteen inches of remaining material should hang down over each side so the Tabernacle is fully covered.
26.14: Top it off with a protective layer of tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather.
26.15: For the Tabernacle's framework, use acacia wood to make frames.
26.16: Each frame should be 15 feet high and 27 inches wide.
26.17: Put two pegs under each frame to keep 'em stable.
26.18: Make twenty frames for the south side of the Tabernacle.
26.19: Then make forty silver bases—two under each frame—so the pegs fit in solid.
26.20: For the north side, do the same thing: twenty frames
26.21: And forty silver bases—two under each frame.
26.22: For the back (west side), make six frames.
26.23: And add two extra frames for the rear corners.
26.24: The corner frames should be matched at the bottom and firmly connected at the top by a single ring.
26.25: So, all together, there'll be eight frames at the rear, set in sixteen silver bases—two bases per frame.
26.26: Make crossbars outta acacia wood to link the frames together—five for the north side
26.27: And five for the south side, plus five for the back (west side).
26.28: The middle crossbar should run the full length of the Tabernacle, halfway up the frames.
26.29: Overlay the frames with gold, and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Then cover the crossbars with gold too.
26.30: Set up the Tabernacle exactly like the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
26.31: Make a special curtain for inside the Tabernacle, woven from fine linen with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, decorated with embroidered cherubim.
26.32: Hang it on gold hooks attached to four acacia wood posts, which should be overlaid with gold and set in silver bases.
26.33: Hang the inner curtain from the clasps and put the Ark of the Covenant behind it. This curtain separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
26.34: Then put the Ark's cover—the Mercy Seat—on top of the Ark inside the Most Holy Place.
26.35: Set the table outside the inner curtain on the north side, and the lampstand across from it on the south side.
26.36: Make another curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle. It should be finely woven linen with exquisite embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
26.37: Craft five acacia wood posts, overlay 'em with gold, and hang the curtain from 'em using gold hooks. Then cast five bronze bases for the posts.

27.1: Take some acacia wood and build a square altar—7.5 feet wide, 7.5 feet long, and 4.5 feet high.
27.2: Make horns for each of its four corners, all one piece with the altar. Then overlay the whole thing with bronze.
27.3: Make ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans—all outta bronze.
27.4: Make a bronze grating for it, and attach four bronze rings at its four corners.
27.5: Put the grating halfway down the side of the altar, right under the ledge.
27.6: For carrying the altar, make some poles from acacia wood, and overlay 'em with bronze.
27.7: Slide those poles through the rings on both sides of the altar.
27.8: The altar gotta be hollow, made from wooden planks. Follow the exact instructions I gave you on the mountain.
27.9: Build a courtyard for the Tabernacle, enclosed by curtains made of fine woven linen. On the south side, make the curtains 150 feet long.
27.10: Hold 'em up with twenty posts set in twenty bronze bases. Hang the curtains with silver hooks and rings.
27.11: Do the same thing on the north side—150 feet of curtains, held up by twenty posts set in bronze bases with silver hooks and rings.
27.12: For the west end, the curtains should be 75 feet long, supported by ten posts set in ten bases.
27.13: The east end—the front of the courtyard—should also be 75 feet long.
27.14: The entrance will be on the east end, flanked by two curtains. The curtain on the right side should be 22.5 feet long, held up by three posts with three bases.
27.15: The curtain on the left side should also be 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts with three bases.
27.16: For the entrance curtain, make it 30 feet long, woven from fine linen with beautiful embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet thread. Support it with four posts, each set in its own base.
27.17: All the courtyard posts should have silver rings and hooks and bronze bases.
27.18: The whole courtyard should be 150 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 7.5 feet high. The walls should be woven linen, and the bases should be bronze.
27.19: All the articles used in Tabernacle rituals—even the tent pegs holding up the Tabernacle and courtyard curtains—must be made of bronze.
27.20: Tell the people to bring you pure pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning all night.
27.21: The lampstand should be inside the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that covers the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron and his sons gotta keep the lamps burning in God's presence all night long. This rule never changes—it's for every generation of Israel.

28.1: Tell your brother Aaron and his sons—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar—to step apart from everybody else so they can serve as my priests.
28.2: Make some fresh, holy garments for Aaron—something glorious and beautiful.
28.3: I already put skill and wisdom in certain artisans, so tell them to make priestly garments that'll show Aaron's been set apart for my work.
28.4: These are the garments they gotta make: a chestpiece, an ephod, a robe, a patterned tunic, a turban, and a sash. They making these for Aaron and his sons to wear when they serve me.
28.5: Use fine linen, gold thread, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
28.6: Make the ephod outta fine linen and skillfully embroider it with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
28.7: It's two pieces—front and back—joined at the shoulders.
28.8: The sash should match—woven linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet.
28.9: Get two onyx stones and engrave the names of Israel's tribes on 'em.
28.10: Six names on each stone, in the birth order of Jacob's sons.
28.11: Engrave them like a jeweler engraves a seal, then mount them in gold settings.
28.12: Fasten these two stones on the shoulders of the ephod—so every time Aaron steps up, he represents Israel.
28.14: Braid two cords of pure gold and attach them to the gold settings on the shoulders.
28.15: Make a chestpiece—a special decision piece—that matches the ephod. Use woven linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
28.16: Make it one piece, folded into a square, about 9 inches on each side.
28.17: Mount four rows of gemstones on it. First row: red carnelian, pale-green peridot, and an emerald.
28.18: Second row: turquoise, lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.
28.19: Third row: orange jacinth, agate, and a purple amethyst.
28.20: Fourth row: blue-green beryl, onyx, and green jasper. Set them all in gold filigree.
28.21: Each stone represents a tribe of Israel, with their name engraved like a seal.
28.22: To attach the chestpiece, make braided cords of pure gold.
28.23: Make two gold rings and attach them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
28.24: Tie the gold cords to those two rings.
28.25: Tie the other ends to the gold settings on the shoulders of the ephod.
28.26: Make two more gold rings and attach 'em to the inside edges of the chestpiece, right next to the ephod.
28.27: Then make two more gold rings on the front of the ephod, below the shoulders, above where the sash ties up.
28.28: Attach the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the ephod's rings with blue cords, keeping it secure.
28.29: So whenever Aaron goes into the Holy Place, he got Israel's names over his heart—a reminder he's reppin' them before the Lord.
28.30: Slide the Urim and Thummim into the chestpiece so they stay over Aaron's heart—that's how he'll seek the Lord's decisions for Israel.
28.31: Make a robe for the ephod, from a single piece of blue cloth.
28.32: Put a reinforced collar in the middle so it won't tear.
28.33: Make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and put them on the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.
28.34: Gold bells, pomegranates, gold bells, pomegranates—all around the hem.
28.35: Aaron gotta wear this robe whenever he steps before the Lord. The bells will ring, letting folks know he's moving in and out the Holy Place—so he don't drop dead.
28.36: Now make a gold medallion, and engrave it like a seal: 'Holy to the Lord.'
28.37: Tie it with a blue cord to the front of Aaron's turban, where it stays.
28.38: Aaron gotta wear it on his forehead, so he can take on Israel's guilt when they bring their sacred offerings. That way, the Lord will accept the people's sacrifices.
28.39: Weave Aaron's patterned tunic from fine linen. Make his turban from linen, and embroider his sash with colors.
28.40: For Aaron's sons, make tunics, sashes, and head coverings—they should look glorious and beautiful.
28.41: Put them on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint 'em and ordain 'em. Consecrate them so they can serve as priests.
28.42: Make some linen undergarments for them to wear next to their skin—from their hips to their thighs.
28.43: They must wear these every time they step into the Tabernacle or come near the altar. Otherwise, they'll die from guilt. This law never changes—it's forever for Aaron and his sons.

29.1: Here's how you set apart Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests: Bring a young bull and two perfect rams.
29.2: Then make some bread, thin cakes, and wafers—all without yeast—and mix 'em with olive oil.
29.3: Put 'em in a basket, and bring 'em to the Tabernacle, along with the bull and the two rams.
29.4: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tabernacle and wash 'em with water.
29.5: Put Aaron's priestly robes on him—the tunic, robe, ephod, and chestpiece—then wrap the decorative sash around him.
29.6: Put the turban on his head and fasten the sacred medallion on it.
29.7: Take the anointing oil and pour it over his head. That's how you set him apart.
29.8: Next, bring in Aaron's sons, and put their tunics on 'em.
29.9: Tie their sashes around their waists and put on their head coverings. The priesthood belongs to them forever—this is how you ordain them.
29.10: Bring the young bull to the entrance of the Tabernacle, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
29.11: Then slaughter the bull in the Lord's presence at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
29.12: Take some of its blood, put it on the horns of the altar, and pour out the rest at the base of the altar.
29.13: Gather up the fat from the organs, the liver lobe, and the kidneys, then burn it all on the altar.
29.14: But take the rest of the bull—its hide, meat, and dung— and burn it outside the camp as a sin offering.
29.15: Now bring one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
29.16: Slaughter the ram, and splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.
29.17: Cut it into pieces, wash the organs and legs, and set 'em next to the head and body pieces.
29.18: Then burn the entire ram on the altar. This is a burnt offering to the Lord—a pleasing aroma, a special gift.
29.19: Now bring the other ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
29.20: Slaughter it, then take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe of Aaron and his sons. Splatter the rest on all sides of the altar.
29.21: Take some of the blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron, his sons, and their garments. That's how you set them apart as holy.
29.22: Since this is the ordination ram, take its fat, fat tail, fat from the organs, the liver lobe, the kidneys, and the right thigh.
29.23: Take one loaf, one thin cake, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord.
29.24: Put all these in Aaron and his sons' hands, and have them lift them up as a special offering to the Lord.
29.25: Then take the bread and meat and burn them on the altar with the burnt offering—a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
29.26: Take the breast of Aaron's ordination ram, lift it up before the Lord, and then keep it as your portion.
29.27: Set aside the breast and thigh of Aaron's ordination ram—they belong to Aaron and his sons.
29.28: From now on, whenever Israel brings a peace offering, a portion belongs to Aaron and his descendants—this is a sacred offering forever.
29.29: Aaron's sacred garments must be passed down to his descendants, so they wear 'em when they get anointed and ordained.
29.30: Whoever becomes high priest after Aaron must wear these for seven days when they minister in the Holy Place.
29.31: Take the ordination ram, and boil its meat in a sacred place.
29.32: Aaron and his sons will eat this meat with the bread from the ordination basket.
29.33: Nobody else can eat it—this is their sacred portion.
29.34: If any of the meat or bread is left by morning, burn it—nobody can eat it.
29.35: Ordain Aaron and his sons for seven days, just like this.
29.36: Each day, sacrifice a young bull as a sin offering to purify them before the Lord.
29.37: Consecrate the altar for seven days. After that, it'll be completely holy, and whatever touches it will become holy.
29.38: Each day, offer two lambs, one in the morning, one in the evening.
29.39: One in the morning, one in the evening—every single day.
29.40: With each lamb, bring two quarts of flour, mixed with a quart of olive oil, plus a quart of wine as a drink offering.
29.41: Do the same thing in the evening—this is a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
29.42: This must be a permanent daily offering for generations to come.
29.43: I'll meet with Israel right there, and my presence will make the place holy.
29.44: I will consecrate the Tabernacle, the altar, Aaron, and his sons so they can serve me as priests.
29.45: Then I will live among the Israelites and be their God.
29.46: They will know I am the Lord who brought them out of Egypt, just so I could live among them. I am the Lord their God.

30.1: Make another altar outta acacia wood for burnin' incense.
30.2: Make it 18 inches square & 36 inches tall, with horns on the corners, all carved from the same piece of wood.
30.3: Overlay it with gold—the top, sides, and horns—and put a gold molding around it.
30.4: Make two gold rings, attach 'em on opposite sides below the molding to hold the carrying poles.
30.5: Make the poles from acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
30.6: Put the altar right outside the inner curtain, in front of the Ark's cover—the place of atonement—where I'll meet with you.
30.7: Every morning, when Aaron fixes the lamps, he gotta burn fragrant incense on this altar.
30.8: And every evening, when he lights the lamps, he gotta burn incense again—this is a permanent rule for all generations.
30.9: Don't burn any unholy incense on this altar—no burnt offerings, grain offerings, or drink offerings either.
30.10: Once a year, Aaron gotta purify the altar by smearing its horns with the blood from the atonement offering. This a regular, annual thing for generations 'cause this is the Lord's most holy altar.
30.12: Every time y'all take a census, each man gotta pay a ransom for himself to the Lord. That way, no plague will hit the people when y'all count 'em.
30.13: Every person who gets counted gotta pay a small silver offering—that's half a shekel (based on the sanctuary's scale, which equals twenty gerahs.)
30.14: Anybody 20 years and older gotta bring this offering to the Lord.
30.15: Don't matter if you rich or poor—everybody pays the same amount to purify their lives before God.
30.16: Take this ransom money and use it for the upkeep of the Tabernacle. This offering will remind the Lord of His people and will purify their lives.
30.18: Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand. Put it between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it up with water.
30.19: Aaron and his sons gotta wash their hands and feet there before entering.
30.20: If they don't wash up before coming into the Lord's presence or offering a sacrifice, they gonna die!
30.21: This rule ain't changing—Aaron and his sons gotta wash up every time from generation to generation.
30.23: Gather these top-tier spices: 12½ pounds of pure myrrh, 6¼ pounds of fragrant cinnamon, 6¼ pounds of fragrant calamus, 12½ pounds of cassia, One gallon of olive oil.
30.24: And grab 12 and a half pounds of cassia—using the sanctuary shekel for weight. Oh, and don't forget to get a full gallon of olive oil too.
30.25: Blend 'em together like a skilled incense maker to create a holy anointing oil.
30.26: Use this oil to anoint the Tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant,
30.27: The table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its accessories, the incense altar,
30.28: The altar of burnt offering and its utensils, and the washbasin with its stand.
30.29: Consecrate them all—make 'em holy so that anything that touches them becomes holy too.
30.30: Anoint Aaron and his sons too—set 'em apart to serve as priests.
30.31: Tell Israel: 'This holy anointing oil is for the Lord alone, forever.
30.32: Don't use it on just anybody. Don't copy this recipe. It's holy, so treat it holy.
30.33: Anybody who makes this oil for personal use or puts it on someone who ain't a priest must be cut off from the people.
30.34: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Gather these fragrant spices: Resin droplets, Mollusk shell, Galbanum, Pure frankincense (weighed out equally)'
30.35: Mix 'em up like a pro incense maker, sprinkle it with salt, and make it a pure & holy incense.
30.36: Grind some up into a fine powder and put it in front of the Ark inside the Tabernacle where I meet with you.
30.37: Don't use this formula for anything else—it's reserved for the Lord alone.
30.38: Anyone who makes this incense for personal use must be cut off from the community.

31.2: 'Look, I picked Bezalel, son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
31.3: I done filled him up with my Spirit, gave him wisdom, skills, & expertise in all kinds of craftsmanship.
31.4: He a master craftsman—knows how to work with gold, silver, & bronze.
31.5: He's skilled in engraving, mounting gemstones, & carving wood—dude got skills in every craft.
31.6: I also picked Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to be his assistant.
31.7: And I done blessed all the gifted craftsmen so they can build everything I told you to make: The Tabernacle, The Ark of the Covenant, The Ark's cover—the place of atonement, All the Tabernacle's furniture
31.8: The table & its utensils, The pure gold lampstand & all its accessories, The incense altar
31.9: The altar for burnt offerings & its utensils, The washbasin & its stand
31.10: The priestly garments—Aaron's sacred outfit & his sons' clothes for serving as priests
31.11: The anointing oil, The fragrant incense for the Holy Place. These craftsmen gon' make everything just like I commanded you.'
31.12: Then the Lord gave Moses another set of instructions:
31.13: 'Tell the people of Israel: Be real careful to keep my Sabbath day—'cause the Sabbath is a sign of my covenant with y'all from generation to generation. It's here so y'all can know I'm the Lord who makes you holy.
31.14: Keep the Sabbath day holy—anybody who disrespects it gotta die. If somebody works on that day, they cut off from the community.
31.15: Y'all got six days every week for work, but the seventh day gotta be a Sabbath—a day fully dedicated to the Lord. Anybody who works on that day gotta be put to death.
31.16: The people of Israel gotta keep the Sabbath, passing it down from generation to generation. It's a covenant law forever.
31.17: This is a permanent sign between me & Israel. 'Cause in six days, the Lord made heaven & earth, but on the seventh day, I chilled & got refreshed.'
31.18: When the Lord finished talking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him two stone tablets—inscribed with the terms of the covenant, written by God's own finger.

32.1: The people started trippin' when they saw Moses takin' too long to come down from the mountain. So they ran up on Aaron and said, 'Yo, make us some gods that can lead us! We dunno what happened to Moses, the dude that brought us outta Egypt.'
32.2: So Aaron was like, 'Aight, take the gold rings from y'all wives, sons, and daughters, and bring 'em to me.'
32.3: Everybody took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
32.4: He melted the gold down, shaped it into a calf, and when they saw it, they started shouting, 'O Israel, these the gods that brought us outta Egypt!'
32.5: Aaron saw how hyped they was, so he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, 'Tomorrow, we havin' a festival for the Lord!'
32.6: Next morning, the people got up early, made sacrifices, feasted, got drunk, and started wildin' out.
32.7: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Get down there—quick! Your people, the ones you brought outta Egypt, already actin' up!'
