32.8: They turned away from me so fast! They melted down gold, made a calf, and now they bowin' down to it, makin' sacrifices, and sayin', 'These are your gods, Israel, the ones that brought you outta Egypt!'
32.9: Then the Lord said, 'Man, I see just how stubborn these people are.'
32.10: 'Now step aside, so I can let my anger loose and wipe 'em all out. Then I'ma start over with you, Moses.'
32.11: But Moses started pleadin' with the Lord, 'Lord, why you so mad at your people, the ones you brought outta Egypt with your power and your strong hand?'
32.12: 'You really gon' let the Egyptians say, "Look at their God—rescued 'em just to wipe 'em out in the mountains!"? Please chill on this anger, Lord, and don't do this to your people!'
32.13: 'Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—you swore to them that you'd make their descendants countless like the stars in the sky, and you'd give them this land forever.'
32.14: So the Lord changed His mind and didn't bring the disaster He threatened on His people.
32.15: Then Moses went down the mountain, holdin' the two stone tablets—the ones God Himself wrote on front & back.
32.16: These weren't just any tablets—they were God's own work, with His words written by His own hand.
32.17: When Joshua heard the noise from the camp, he said, 'Moses, sound like a war goin' on down there!'
32.18: But Moses said, 'Nah, that ain't the sound of victory or defeat—that's celebration.'
32.19: When they got close, Moses saw the golden calf and people dancin' around it—he got heated, threw the stone tablets, and smashed 'em at the mountain's base.
32.20: Then he took the calf, burned it down, crushed it into powder, dumped it in the water, and made everybody drink it.
32.21: Then he turned to Aaron: 'Bruh, what did these people do to you to make you help 'em sin like this?'
32.22: Aaron said, 'Man, chill, you know how these folks stay actin' up.'
32.23: 'They came to me sayin', "Make us some gods to lead us since we dunno what happened to Moses."'
32.24: 'So I told 'em, "Whoever got gold, take it off." They brought it to me, I threw it in the fire, and out came this calf!'
32.25: Moses saw how Aaron let the people go wild, and how their enemies were laughin' at 'em.
32.26: So he stood at the camp entrance and shouted, 'Who rockin' with the Lord, come stand with me!' And all the Levites gathered around him.
32.27: Moses told 'em, 'This is what the Lord says—strap up and go through the camp, takin' out whoever—brothers, friends, neighbors—don't matter.'
32.28: The Levites followed Moses' command, and that day about 3,000 people got put down.
32.29: Then Moses told 'em, 'Today y'all proved y'all stand with the Lord—even though it meant killin' y'all own kin. And today, y'all earned a blessing.'
32.30: Next day, Moses told the people, 'Y'all really messed up bad, but I'ma go back up the mountain—maybe I can beg for forgiveness.'
32.31: So Moses went back up to the Lord and said, 'Lord, these people really did you dirty—they made gods of gold for themselves!'
32.32: 'But if you just forgive them… if not, then just erase my name too.'
32.33: But the Lord said, 'Nah, I only erase the names of those who sinned against me.'
32.34: 'Now lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel gon' lead the way, but when the time comes, I will make them answer for what they did.'
32.35: Then the Lord sent a plague on the people 'cause of the golden calf Aaron made.

33.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, get movin'—you and these people you brought outta Egypt. Head to the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I told them, "I'ma give this land to your descendants."'
33.2: I'ma send an angel ahead of you to clear out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
33.3: Go up to the land flowin' with milk and honey—but I ain't goin' with y'all, 'cause y'all too stubborn and hardheaded. If I roll with you, I'ma end up wipin' y'all out on the way.
33.4: When the people heard this harsh word, they started mourning and stopped flexin' with their jewelry and fine clothes.
33.5: The Lord told Moses to tell them, 'Y'all stubborn and rebellious—if I roll with y'all, even for a second, I'd wipe y'all out. So take off them chains, bracelets, and fancy robes while I figure out what I'ma do with y'all.'
33.6: So from Mount Sinai on, the Israelites ain't rock no jewelry or fancy clothes no more.
33.7: Moses had a habit—he'd take the Tent of Meeting and set it outside the camp, far off. Anybody who needed to holla at the Lord had to go outside the camp to that tent.
33.8: Whenever Moses went to the Tent of Meeting, everybody got up and stood in front of their own tents, watchin' him till he went inside.
33.9: As soon as Moses stepped in, the pillar of cloud would come down and hover at the entrance, and the Lord would talk to Moses.
33.10: When the people saw the cloud chillin' at the entrance, they would stand up and bow in front of their own tents.
33.11: Inside the Tent of Meeting, the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, like somebody talkin' to their homie. Afterward, Moses would go back to the camp, but his assistant Joshua, son of Nun, stayed in the tent.
33.12: One day, Moses told the Lord, 'You been tellin' me, "Lead these people to the land," but you ain't told me who you sendin' with me. You also said, "I know you by name, and I got favor on you."
33.13: So if that's real, Lord, let me understand your ways more, so I can keep walkin' in your favor. And don't forget—this nation is YOUR people.
33.14: The Lord replied, 'Aight, I'ma go with you personally, and I'ma give you rest. Everything gon' be fine.'
33.15: Then Moses said, 'Lord, if you ain't rollin' with us, don't make us leave this place.'
33.16: 'How else anybody gon' know we your people, that you rock with us? Your presence is what makes us different from everybody else on earth!'
33.17: The Lord replied, 'Aight, Moses, I'ma do what you ask, 'cause I got favor on you, and I know you by name.'
33.18: Then Moses said, 'Aight, Lord, let me see your glory!'
33.19: The Lord replied, 'Aight, I'ma let all my goodness pass before you, and I'ma call out my name—Yahweh. I show mercy to whoever I choose and compassion to whoever I choose.'
33.20: 'But you can't look straight at my face, 'cause nobody can see me and live.'
33.21: Then the Lord said, 'Look, stand over here on this rock.'
33.22: 'When my glorious presence passes by, I'ma hide you in the crevice of the rock and cover you with my hand till I'm gone.'
33.23: 'Then I'ma move my hand, and you can see my back, but you ain't gon' see my face.'

34.1: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, carve out two stone tablets, just like the ones you broke. I'ma write down the same words that was on the first set.'
34.2: Be ready by morning to climb Mount Sinai and come meet me at the top.
34.3: Ain't nobody else allowed to come with you—not a soul. Matter fact, don't even let the livestock graze near the mountain.
34.4: So Moses did what God said—chiseled out two stone tablets, got up early in the morning, and climbed Mount Sinai with the tablets in hand.
34.5: Then the Lord came down in a cloud, stood there with Moses, and called out His own name—Yahweh.
34.6: The Lord passed in front of Moses, calling out: 'Yahweh! The Lord! The God of compassion and mercy! I'm slow to anger, full of love, and faithful.
34.7: 'I show unfailing love to a thousand generations. I forgive sin, rebellion, and iniquity, but I don't let the guilty slide. I hold folks accountable, even down to their kids and grandkids.'
34.8: Moses immediately fell on his face and worshiped.
34.9: Then Moses said, 'Lord, if I really got favor with you, please stay with us. Yeah, we hardheaded and rebellious, but please forgive us and claim us as yours.'
34.10: The Lord replied, 'Listen up—I'ma make a covenant with you. I'ma do miracles so wild that no nation has ever seen before. Everybody gon' witness my power.'
34.11: 'Follow everything I command you today. I'ma go ahead of you and push out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
34.12: But don't make no treaties with the people in the land. They'll lead you into their mess and trap you.
34.13: Instead, tear down their altars, smash their pillars, and cut down them Asherah poles.
34.14: You must worship no other gods, 'cause the Lord's name is Jealous—and He don't play about His people.
34.15: Don't make a deal with them folks, 'cause they out here chasing other gods and making sacrifices. They'll invite you to join in, and you gon' go with 'em.
34.16: Then y'all gon' start marrying their daughters, and they gon' pull your sons into their false worship.
34.17: Don't be out here making no metal gods for yourself.
34.18: You must celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread without yeast, just like I told you. Do this every year in early spring 'cause that's when I freed y'all from Egypt.
34.19: Every firstborn belongs to me—human or animal.
34.20: If you got a firstborn donkey, you gotta redeem it with a lamb. If you don't, then break its neck. But all firstborn sons must be redeemed.
34.21: You got six days to work, but on the seventh day, stop—even when it's planting and harvest season.
34.22: Celebrate the Festival of Harvest when y'all bring the first crops. And celebrate the Festival of Final Harvest when everything is gathered up.
34.23: Every man in Israel gotta appear before the Lord three times a year.
34.24: I'ma drive out your enemies and expand your land, and ain't nobody gon' mess with your territory while y'all worship me.
34.25: Don't offer my sacrifice with bread that got yeast in it. And don't keep no Passover meat overnight.
34.26: Bring the best of your first harvest to the Lord's house.
34.27: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Write all this down—this is the covenant I'm making with you and Israel.'
34.28: Moses stayed up there forty days and nights, no food, no water. The Lord wrote down the Ten Commandments on the tablets.
34.29: When Moses came down, holding the stone tablets, he ain't even know his face was glowing 'cause he been talking to the Lord.
34.30: When Aaron and the people saw his face shining, they got shook and didn't wanna come close.
34.31: But Moses called them over. Aaron and the leaders came first, and Moses spoke with them.
34.32: Then all the Israelites came, and Moses gave them all the instructions the Lord had told him.
34.33: Afterwards, Moses put on a veil to cover his face.
34.34: But whenever he went to talk to the Lord, he'd take off the veil till he came back.
34.35: Then he'd give the people God's instructions, and they'd see his face still glowing. So he'd put the veil back on till the next time he went to talk with the Lord.

35.1: Then Moses pulled up on the whole Israelite crew and told 'em, 'Aight y'all, listen up—this what the Lord commanded.'
35.2: 'Y'all got six days to handle your business and do all your work. But on the seventh day, that's the Sabbath—a holy day set aside for the Lord. Anybody who works that day? They gotta be put to death.'
35.3: 'Matter fact, don't even light a fire in ya crib on the Sabbath.'
35.4: Moses kept goin': 'This what the Lord commands y'all to do.
35.5: Everybody whose heart feel moved, bring an offering for the Lord.'
35.6: 'Here's what y'all need to bring: gold, silver, bronze,'
35.7: 'Blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goat hair for makin' cloth.'
35.8: 'Tanned ram skins, fine goatskin leather, and acacia wood.'
35.9: 'Olive oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil, and some good-smellin' incense.'
35.10: 'Onyx stones and other gems to be set in the ephod and priest's chestpiece.'
35.11: 'Now, all y'all skilled craftsmen—get ready to build everything the Lord commanded!'
35.12: 'That means the Tabernacle, its tent, covering, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases.'
35.13: 'The Ark of the Covenant and its carrying poles, plus the atonement cover that go on top of it.'
35.14: 'The inner curtain to shield the Ark.'
35.15: 'The table, its carrying poles, all the utensils, and the Bread of the Presence.'
35.16: 'The lampstand with all its accessories, the lamp cups, and the olive oil for keepin' it lit.'
35.17: 'The incense altar and its carrying poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle.'
35.18: 'The altar of burnt offerings, its bronze grating, all its utensils, and the washbasin with its stand.'
35.19: 'The curtains for the courtyard walls, the posts and bases, and the entrance curtain to the courtyard.'
35.20: 'All the tent pegs for the Tabernacle and courtyard, plus all the ropes. Oh, and don't forget:'
35.21: 'The freshly stitched garments for the priests to wear in the Holy Place—Aaron's sacred clothes and the ones his sons gotta wear while they minister.'
35.22: After Moses finished speaking, everybody headed back to their tents.
35.23: Then everybody whose heart felt stirred came through with their offerings. Folks brought all the materials needed for the Tabernacle, the priestly garments, and all the rituals.
35.24: Men and women, whoever felt moved, pulled up with their gold—brooches, earrings, rings, necklaces—you name it. Everything was given to the Lord.
35.25: If folks had blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, goat hair, tanned ram skins, or fine leather, they brought it.
35.26: Anybody with silver and bronze? They gave it for the Lord. Those with acacia wood brought it too.
35.27: All the women skilled in sewing and spinning got to work, preppin' blue, purple, and scarlet thread, plus fine linen cloth.
35.28: All the women who knew how to spin goat hair into yarn jumped in too.
35.29: The leaders pulled up with onyx stones and special gemstones for the ephod and the priest's chestpiece.
35.30: They also brought spices and olive oil for the lights, anointing oil, and fragrant incense.
35.31: Basically, every man and woman who had it in their heart to give towards the Lord's work brought their gifts willingly. That's how they contributed to the Lord.
35.32: Then Moses told the people, 'Look, the Lord done picked out Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.'
35.33: 'The Lord filled him up with the Holy Spirit, giving him mad wisdom, skill, and talent for all kinds of crafts.
35.34: That boy a master craftsman—expert in gold, silver, and bronze work.'
35.35: 'He's skilled in engraving, gem-setting, wood-carving, and basically any creative work.'
35.36: 'But Bezalel ain't the only one—Oholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, got that same anointing too. Plus, the Lord gave them the ability to teach others.'
35.37: 'God gave 'em special skills—engraving, designing, embroidering blue, purple, and scarlet thread on fine linen—and weaving. These dudes got the gift for craftsmanship and designing.'

36.1: The Lord gave Bezalel, Oholiab, and the rest of the skilled craftsmen wisdom and ability to do the work needed to build up the Lord's sanctuary. They gotta construct and furnish the Tabernacle just like the Lord commanded.
36.2: So Moses called up Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the skilled folks the Lord blessed who was eager to work.
36.3: Moses handed them all the materials the Israelites brought as offerings for the sanctuary. But the people kept bringing more gifts every morning.
36.4: Finally, the craftsmen stopped working and went to Moses.
36.5: They said, 'Look, the people brought more than enough to get this job done just like the Lord commanded.'
36.6: So Moses gave the order and spread the word through the camp: 'Aight y'all, stop bringing gifts. We good!'
36.7: The offerings they got was more than enough to finish the whole project.
36.8: The skilled craftsmen made ten curtains of fine linen, decorated with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, embroidered with cherubim.
36.9: All ten curtains was the same size—42 feet long & 6 feet wide.
36.10: They linked five curtains together to make one long piece, then did the same for the other five.
36.11: He made fifty loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in each set.
36.12: The fifty loops on one side lined up perfectly with the fifty loops on the other side.
36.13: Then he made fifty gold clasps to fasten the curtains together, making the Tabernacle one continuous piece.
36.14: He made eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as a tent covering for the Tabernacle.
36.15: Each of these eleven curtains was 45 feet long & 6 feet wide.
36.16: He joined five curtains together for one long piece and six curtains for another.
36.17: Fifty loops were made along the edges of each big curtain.
36.18: Then he made fifty bronze clasps to fasten 'em together, making one solid covering.
36.19: To top it off, he made a layer of tanned ram skins and a fine goatskin leather cover.
36.20: Bezalel built the frames of acacia wood.
36.21: Each frame stood 15 feet tall & 27 inches wide.
36.22: Each frame had two pegs at the bottom, and all of them was built the same way.
36.23: He made twenty frames for the south side of the Tabernacle.
36.24: He also made forty silver bases—two bases per frame to hold 'em in place.
36.25: For the north side, he made twenty more frames.
36.26: He made forty silver bases for them too—two per frame.
36.27: He made six frames for the rear (west side) of the Tabernacle.
36.28: Then he made two extra corner frames for reinforcement.
36.29: These corner frames was built as one solid unit, attached at the top & bottom with a single ring.
36.30: So in the back, the Tabernacle had eight frames set in sixteen silver bases—two per frame.
36.31: Then he made crossbars from acacia wood to link the frames—five for each side.
36.32: Five went on the north side, five on the south, and five on the rear side (west).
36.33: He made the middle crossbar to run from one end to the other.
36.34: All the frames was covered in gold, with gold rings to hold the crossbars.
36.35: Inside the Tabernacle, he made a special curtain of fine linen, embroidered with cherubim using blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
36.36: To hold it up, he made four acacia posts with gold hooks, set in silver bases.
36.37: For the entrance curtain, he made it from fine linen and embroidered it with designs in blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
36.38: This curtain hung on gold hooks, attached to five acacia posts, with gold tops and bronze bases.

37.1: Then Bezalel made the Ark of the Covenant out of acacia wood—a sacred chest 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high.
37.2: He coated it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold trim around the edges.
37.3: Then he cast four gold rings and attached them to its four feet—two rings on each side.
37.4: He made poles from acacia wood and covered them in gold.
37.5: Then he slid the poles into the rings on the sides of the Ark, so it could be carried.
37.6: Next, he made the Ark's cover—aka the atonement cover—from pure gold, 45 inches long and 27 inches wide.
37.7: He sculpted two cherubim from hammered gold and put them on opposite ends of the atonement cover.
37.8: The cherubim were molded as one piece with the cover, their wings spread out over it.
37.9: They faced each other and looked down at the atonement cover, with their wings covering it protectively.
37.10: Then Bezalel made the table from acacia wood—36 inches long, 18 inches wide, and 27 inches high.
37.11: He covered it in pure gold and added a gold trim around the edges.
37.12: He decorated it with a 3-inch border and put gold molding around it.
37.13: Then he cast four gold rings and attached them at the four corners near the legs.
37.14: The rings were placed near the border, so they could hold the carrying poles.
37.15: He made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold.
37.16: Then he made special containers for the table—bowls, ladles, jars, and pitchers—all from pure gold, to be used for liquid offerings.
37.17: Then Bezalel made the lampstand from pure, hammered gold—a single piece including the base, center stem, lamp cups, buds, and petals.
37.18: The lampstand had six branches—three on each side.
37.19: Each of the six branches had three lamp cups, shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.
37.20: The center stem had four lamp cups, also shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
37.21: There was an almond bud under each pair of branches, all made from one piece.
37.22: Everything—the almond buds, branches, and center stem—was crafted as a single piece from hammered pure gold.
37.23: He also made seven lamps for the lampstand, plus lamp snuffers and trays—all from pure gold.
37.24: The whole lampstand and its accessories were made from 75 pounds of pure gold.
37.25: Then Bezalel made the incense altar from acacia wood—18 inches square and 36 inches high—with horns carved from the same piece.
37.26: He coated the top, sides, and horns in pure gold and added a gold molding around the whole thing.
37.27: Then he made two gold rings and attached them on opposite sides below the gold molding—these were for the carrying poles.
37.28: He made poles from acacia wood and covered them in gold.
37.29: Then he made the sacred anointing oil and the fragrant incense, using the techniques of a skilled incense maker.

38.1: Then Bezalel built the altar for burnt offerings out of acacia wood—a square altar, 7.5 feet wide, 7.5 feet long, and 4.5 feet high.
38.2: He carved horns on each of the four corners, making them one solid piece with the altar, then coated the whole thing in bronze.
38.3: He made all the altar tools out of bronze—the ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans.
38.4: Then he made a bronze grating and put it halfway down the side of the altar, under the ledge.
38.5: He cast four rings and attached them to the corners of the bronze grating to hold the carrying poles.
38.6: He made the poles from acacia wood and coated them with bronze.
38.7: Then he slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so it could be carried easily.
38.8: The altar was hollow, made out of wooden planks.
38.9: Then Bezalel made the bronze washbasin and its stand from bronze mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
38.10: Then Bezalel built the courtyard around the Tabernacle, enclosing it with curtains made of fine woven linen. The south side curtains were 150 feet long.
38.11: He set up twenty posts, each one securely placed in a bronze base. He hung the curtains with silver hooks and rings.
38.12: He built the north side the same way—150 feet of curtains hung on twenty posts with bronze bases, silver hooks, and rings.
38.13: The west side of the courtyard was 75 feet long, supported by ten posts in ten bases, hung with silver hooks and rings.
38.14: The east side—the front entrance—was also 75 feet long.
38.15: The courtyard entrance had two curtains, one on each side. The right-side curtain was 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts in three bases.
38.16: The left-side curtain was also 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts in three bases.
38.17: All the curtains in the courtyard were made of fine woven linen.
38.18: Each post had a bronze base, with silver hooks and rings. The tops of the posts were covered in silver, and the curtain rings were also silver.
38.19: He made the entrance curtain for the courtyard out of fine woven linen and embroidered it with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
38.20: The entrance curtain was 30 feet long and 7.5 feet high, just like the other courtyard walls.
38.21: It was held up by four posts, each set into its own bronze base. The tops of the posts were covered in silver, and the hooks and rings were silver too.
38.22: All the tent pegs used for the Tabernacle and courtyard were made of bronze.
38.23: This is the inventory list for everything used in building the Tabernacle of the Covenant. The Levites put it together, following Moses' instructions, and Ithamar (Aaron's son) was in charge of keeping records.
38.24: Bezalel, son of Uri (grandson of Hur), from the tribe of Judah, made everything the Lord commanded Moses.
38.25: Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, was his assistant—a skilled engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet thread on fine linen.
38.26: The people donated 2,193 pounds of gold for the Tabernacle, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
38.27: The whole Israelite community donated 7,545 pounds of silver, also measured by the sanctuary shekel.
38.28: This silver came from the tax collected from each man counted in the census—one beka per person (half a shekel, measured by the sanctuary shekel). It was collected from 603,550 men, all 20 years or older.
38.29: A total of 7,500 pounds of silver was used for the 100 bases of the sanctuary walls and the inner curtain posts—75 pounds per base.
38.30: The remaining 45 pounds of silver was used for hooks, rings, and silver overlays for the post tops.
38.31: The people also brought 5,310 pounds of bronze as a special offering.
38.32: This bronze was used to cast the bases for the posts at the entrance of the Tabernacle and to make the bronze altar with its grating and utensils.
38.33: Bronze was also used for the bases of the courtyard posts, the bases of the entrance curtain posts, and all the tent pegs for the Tabernacle and courtyard.

39.1: The skilled craftsmen made the sacred garments from blue, purple, and scarlet cloth—these were the special clothes Aaron wore when he worked in the Holy Place, just like the Lord told Moses.
39.2: Bezalel made the ephod from fine linen and embroidered it with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
39.3: He made gold thread by hammering out thin sheets of gold, cutting them into fine strands, and weaving them into the fabric with the blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
39.4: The ephod had two parts, one in the front and one in the back, joined together at the shoulders.
39.5: The decorative sash was made from the same material—fine linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
39.6: They mounted two onyx stones in gold settings and engraved them with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, just like a jeweler engraves a seal.
39.7: They attached these stones to the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as a reminder that the priest represents Israel whenever he comes before the Lord. Everything was done just like the Lord told Moses.
39.8: Bezalel made the chestpiece with great skill, to match the ephod, using fine linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
39.9: The chestpiece was made as one single piece of fabric, folded to form a pouch, measuring 9 inches square.
39.10: He mounted four rows of gemstones on it. The first row had a red carnelian, a pale-green peridot, and an emerald.
39.11: The second row had a turquoise, a lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.
39.12: The third row had an orange jacinth, an agate, and a purple amethyst.
39.13: The fourth row had a blue-green beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper.
39.14: Each stone represented one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and their names were engraved like a seal.
39.15: To attach the chestpiece to the ephod, they made braided cords of pure gold.
39.16: They also made two settings of gold filigree and two gold rings, attaching them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
39.17: They tied the gold cords to the rings on the chestpiece.
39.18: The other ends of the gold cords were tied to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.
39.19: They made two more gold rings and attached them to the inside edges of the chestpiece, next to the ephod.
39.20: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the front of the ephod, just below the shoulder-pieces, above the decorative sash.
39.21: They attached the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod with blue cords. This way, the chestpiece stayed securely in place. Everything was done just like the Lord told Moses.
39.22: Bezalel made the robe that went with the ephod from one solid piece of blue woven cloth.
39.23: The robe had a hole for Aaron's head, reinforced with a woven collar so it wouldn't tear.
39.24: They decorated the hem of the robe with pomegranates made from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
39.25: They made gold bells and placed them between the pomegranates along the hem of the robe.
39.26: The bells and pomegranates alternated all around the hem. This robe was worn whenever Aaron ministered before the Lord, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
39.27: They made tunics for Aaron and his sons from fine linen cloth.
39.28: They made the turban and special head coverings from fine linen. The undergarments were also made from finely woven linen.
39.29: They made the sashes from fine linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
39.30: Finally, they made the sacred medallion—the badge of holiness—out of pure gold.
39.31: They engraved it like a seal with the words: "Holy to the Lord."
39.32: They attached the medallion to Aaron's turban with a blue cord, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
39.33: Finally, the Tabernacle was finished. The Israelites did everything exactly the way the Lord commanded Moses.
39.34: They brought everything to Moses: The sacred tent with all its furnishings, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases. The tent coverings of tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather. The inner curtain to shield the Ark.
39.35: The Ark of the Covenant and its carrying poles.
39.36: The Ark's cover—the place of atonement.
39.37: The table and all its utensils.
39.39: The pure gold lampstand with its symmetrical lamp cups, accessories, and olive oil for lighting.
39.41: The anointing oil and fragrant incense.
39.42: The curtain for the entrance of the sacred tent.
39.43: The bronze altar, the bronze grating, its carrying poles and utensils.
39.45: The curtains for the walls of the courtyard.
39.47: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard.
39.49: All the furnishings used for worship in the Tabernacle.
39.50: The beautifully stitched garments for the priests to wear while serving in the Holy Place—including the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and his sons.
39.51: So the people of Israel followed all the Lord's instructions to Moses.
39.52: Then Moses inspected everything, and when he saw that it had all been done exactly as the Lord commanded, he blessed them.

40.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
40.2: "On the first day of the new year, set up the Tabernacle."
40.3: "Put the Ark of the Covenant inside, and hang up the inner curtain to enclose the Ark inside the Most Holy Place."
40.4: "Bring in the table, arrange the utensils, and set up the lampstand with the lamps."
40.5: "Place the gold incense altar in front of the Ark of the Covenant, then hang the curtain at the entrance of the Tabernacle."
40.6: "Put the altar of burnt offering in front of the Tabernacle entrance."
40.7: "Set the washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it up with water."
40.8: "Then set up the courtyard all around the outside of the tent, and hang the curtain for the courtyard entrance."
40.9: "Take the anointing oil and anoint the Tabernacle and everything inside to set them apart as holy."
40.10: "Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils to consecrate them. Then the altar will become completely holy."
40.11: "Anoint the washbasin and its stand, and set them apart as holy."
40.12: "Bring Aaron and his sons to the Tabernacle entrance, and wash them with water."
40.13: "Dress Aaron in his priestly garments, anoint him, and consecrate him to serve as priest."
40.14: "Then bring his sons, dress them in their tunics,"
40.15: "Anoint them just like their father, so they too may serve as priests. With this anointing, the priesthood will be set apart for Aaron's family forever."
40.16: Moses did everything exactly the way the Lord commanded.
40.17: So, on the first day of the first month, in the second year, the Tabernacle was set up.
40.18: Moses set down the bases, raised up the frames, attached the crossbars, and set up the posts.
40.19: Then he spread out the coverings over the Tabernacle and put on the protective layers, just as the Lord had commanded.
40.20: He took the stone tablets with the covenant terms and put them inside the Ark of the Covenant.
40.21: Then he brought the Ark into the Tabernacle and hung the inner curtain, shielding it from view, just as the Lord commanded.
40.22: Moses put the table in the Tabernacle, on the north side outside the inner curtain.
40.23: He arranged the Bread of the Presence on the table before the Lord, just as the Lord commanded.
40.24: He set up the lampstand across from the table, on the south side of the Holy Place.
40.25: Then he lit the lamps in the Lord's presence, just like the Lord commanded.
40.26: He placed the gold incense altar inside the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain.
40.27: Then he burned fragrant incense on it, just like the Lord commanded.
40.28: He hung up the curtain at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
40.29: Moses placed the altar of burnt offering near the Tabernacle entrance.
40.30: Then he put the washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar, filling it with water for the priests to wash themselves.
40.31: Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons washed their hands and feet from the washbasin.
40.32: Whenever they approached the altar or entered the Tabernacle, they washed themselves, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
40.33: Then he hung the curtains around the courtyard and put up the curtain at the entrance. At last, Moses finished the work.
40.34: Then the cloud covered the Tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord filled the whole place.
40.35: Moses couldn't enter the Tabernacle, because the cloud had settled over it, and the Lord's glory filled it up.
40.36: Whenever the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle, the people of Israel would set out and continue their journey.
40.37: But if the cloud didn't rise, they stayed where they were until it did.
40.38: The cloud of the Lord hovered over the Tabernacle by day, and at night it glowed like fire so that all the Israelites could see it. This continued throughout all their journeys.
